questions.q:
A parallel plate capacitor was made with two rectangular plates, each with a length of $l=3 \mathrm{~cm}$ and breath of $\mathrm{b}=1 \mathrm{~cm}$. The distance between the plates is $3 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. Out of the following, which are the ways to increase the capacitance by a factor of 10 ?
A. $l=30 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~b}=1 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~d}=1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$
B. $l=3 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~b}=1 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~d}=30 \mu \mathrm{~m}$
C. $l=6 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~b}=5 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~d}=3 \mu \mathrm{~m}$
D. $l=1 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~b}=1 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~d}=10 \mu \mathrm{~m}$
E. $l=5 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~b}=2 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{~d}=1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: We know $C=\frac{A \varepsilon_0}{d}=\frac{b \ell \varepsilon_0}{d}$ So to increase the capacitance by 10 factor \left(\frac{A}{d}\right)$ has to increase by 10 fator. For option (A) $\quad C^{\prime}=\frac{(30 \ell) b \varepsilon_0}{\left(\frac{d}{3}\right)}=30 \mathrm{C}$ For option (B) $\quad C^{\prime}=\frac{\ell b \varepsilon_0}{10 d}=\frac{C}{10}$ For option (C) $\quad C^{\prime}=\frac{(2 \ell) 5 b \varepsilon_0}{d}=10 \mathrm{C}$ For option (D) $\quad C^{\prime}=\frac{\left(\frac{\ell}{3}\right) b \varepsilon_0}{\left(\frac{10 d}{3}\right)}=\frac{C}{10}$ For option (E) $\quad C^{\prime}=\frac{\left(\frac{\ell}{3}\right) 5(2 b) \varepsilon_0}{\left(\frac{d}{3}\right)}=10 C$ Clearly (C) and (E) are the situation for 10 C$

questions.q: A capacitor is made of a flat plate of area A and a second plate having a stair-like structure as shown in figure. If the area of each stair is $\frac{A}{3}$ and the height is $d$, the capacitance of the arrangement is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
All capacitor are in parallel combination.
Also effective area is common area only
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow C_{\text {eq }}=C_1+C_2+C_3 \\ & \Rightarrow C_{\text {eq }}=\frac{A \varepsilon_0}{3 d}+\frac{A \varepsilon_0}{3(2 d)}+\frac{A \varepsilon_0}{3(3 d)} \\ & \Rightarrow C_{\text {eq }}=\frac{A \varepsilon_0}{3}\left(\frac{11}{6 d}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow C_{\text {eq }}=\frac{11 A \varepsilon_0}{18 d}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A parallel plate capacitor is formed by two plates each of area $30\pi{cm}^{2}$ separated by $1$ mm. A material of dielectric strength $3 . 6 \times {10}^{7}Vm^{- 1}$ is filled between the plates. If the maximum charge that can be stored on the capacitor without causing any dielectric breakdown is $7 \times {10}^{- 6}C$, the value of dielectric constant of the material is :

[Use $\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{o}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{2}C^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The dielectric strength given is& $3 . 6 \times {10}^{7}Vm^{- 1}$.and the separation is~$1$ mm. Therefore, maximum potential difference that can be applied will be,

${V}_\max = 3 . 6 \times {10}^{7} \times d$.

Now,

$C = \dfrac{qmax}{Vmax} ⇒ \dfrac{k{ε}_{0}A}{d} = \dfrac{7 \times {10}^{- 7}}{3 . 6 \times {10}^{7} \times d}k = \dfrac{d}{{ε}_{0} \times 30\pi \times {10}^{- 4}} \times \dfrac{7 \times {10}^{- 7}}{3 . 6 \times {10}^{7} \times d} = 2 . 33$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $2F$ is charged to a potential $V$. The energy stored in the capacitor is ${E}_{1}$. The capacitor is now connected to another uncharged identical capacitor in parallel combination. The energy stored in the combination is ${E}_{2}$. The ratio $\dfrac{E2}{E1}$& is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The charge on the plates of the first capacitor when connected against the potential difference& $V$~is given by

$\begin{cases}Q & = & CV \\ = & 2V\end{cases}$

When both the capacitors are connected, from the conservation of charge, it can be written that

$\begin{cases}2V & = & 2V^{'} + 2V^{'} \\ ⇒ & V^{'} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}V\right)\end{cases}$

where,~$V '$~is the new potential difference across each capacitor.

The formula to calculate the energy stored in the first capacitor is given by

$\begin{cases}{E}_{1} & = & \dfrac{1}{2} \times C \times V^{2} \\ = & \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times V^{2} \\ = & V^{2} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

For the second case, the energy stored in the combination of capacitor is given by

$\begin{cases}{E}_{2} & = & \dfrac{1}{2}nCV{'}^{2} \\ = & \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times \dfrac{V2}{4} \times 2 \\ = & \left(\dfrac{V2}{2}\right) . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) to obtain the required ratio of the stored energy.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{E2}{E1} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{V2}{2}}{V2} \\ = & \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\end{cases}$

questions.q: The parallel combination of two air filled parallel plate capacitors of capacitance $C$ and $nC$ is connected to a battery of voltage, $V .$ When the capacitors are fully charged, the battery is removed and after that a dielectric material of dielectric constant $K$ is placed the two plates of the first capacitor. The new potential difference of the combined system is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
i)

ii) Battery disconnected after full charge,
Total charge of the system,
$= CV + nCV$
$= \left(n + 1\right)CV$

iii) Inserting dielectric of constant $K$

Common potential, ${V}_{C} = \dfrac{totalcharge}{totalcapacitance}$
$= \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)CV}{KC + nC} = \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)V}{K + n}$

questions.q:
A slab of dielectric constant $K$ has the same crosssectional area as the plates of a parallel plate capacitor and thickness $\dfrac{3}{4}d$, where $d$ is the separation of the plates. The capacitance of the capacitor when the slab is inserted between the plates will be :
(Given ${C}_{0} =$ capacitance of capacitor with air as medium between plates.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the above diagram, we can write,

$x + y + \dfrac{3d}{4} = d$

$x + y = \dfrac{d}{4}$

Initially, when there is no dielectric inserted between the plates the capacitance will be,~${C}_{0} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{d}$.

When the dielectric slab is inserted, we can assume there are~$3$~capacitors that are connected in series.

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{x}$,~${C}_{2} = \dfrac{4K{ϵ}_{0}A}{3d}$~and~${C}_{3} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{y}$

The equivalent capacitance,

$\dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{C1} + \dfrac{1}{C2} + \dfrac{1}{C3} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{ϵ}_{0}A}\left(x + \dfrac{3d}{4K} + y\right) ⇒ \dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{ϵ}_{0}A}\left(\dfrac{d}{4} + \dfrac{3d}{4K}\right) ⇒ C = \dfrac{4{ϵ}_{0}AK}{d\left(3 + K\right)} ⇒ C = \dfrac{4K{C}_{0}}{3 + K}$

questions.q: Consider the combination of two& capacitors ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$, with ${C}_{2} > {C}_{1}$, when connected in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is $10$ times the equivalent capacitance of the same connected in series. Calculate the ratio of capacitors, $\dfrac{C2}{C1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$When connected in parallel

${C}_{eq} = {C}_{1} + {C}_{2}$

When in series

${C}_{eq}^{'} = \dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}}$

${C}_{1} + {C}_{2} = 10 \left(\dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}}\right)$

\left({C}_{1} + {C}_{2}\right)2 = 10{C}_{1}{C}_{2}$

${C}_{1}^{2} + {C}_{2}^{2} - 8{C}_{1}{C}_{2} = 0$

dividing by ${C}_{1}^{2}$

$\$left(\dfrac{C2}{C1}\right)2 - \dfrac{8{C}_{2}}{C1} +1 = 0$

Let $\dfrac{C2}{C1} =x$

$x^{2} - 8x + 1 = 0$

$x = \dfrac{8 \pm \sqrt{64 - 4}}{2} =4 + \sqrt{15}$

This question was Bonus in JEE Main 2021 exam because of incorrect data in original question.

$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is filled equally (half) with two dielectrics of dielectric constant $\varepsilon_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$, as shown in figures. The distance between the plates is d and area of each plate is A. If capacitance in first configuration and second configuration are $C_1$ and $C_2$ respectively, then $\frac{C_1}{C_2}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Area of plate is $A$. then
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{C}=\frac{\varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d} / 2}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}} \\ & \mathrmC^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d} / 2}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}
\end{aligned}$
Let $\mathrm{C}_0=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{C}=2 \varepsilon_2 \mathrm{C}_0 \\ & \mathrmC^{\prime}=2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0
\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{C} \ \text{ and } \mathrmC^{\prime}$ are in series
$\mathrm{C}_1=\frac{\mathrm{CC}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{C}+\mathrmC^{\prime}}=\frac{4 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_0\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)}$
$=\frac{2 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0}{\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)}$
Here $\mathrm{C}=\frac{\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{2 \mathrm{~d}}=\frac{\varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0}{2}$
$\mathrmC^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_2 \mathrm{C}_0}{2}$
$\mathrm{C} \ \text{ and } \mathrmC^{\prime}$ are inparallel
$\mathrm{C}_2=\mathrmC^{\prime}+\mathrm{C}=\left(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2\right) \frac{\mathrm{C}_0}{2}$
Thus $\frac{\mathrm{C}_1}{\mathrm{C}_2}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0}{\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)} \times \frac{2}{\left(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2\right) \mathrm{C}_0}$
$=\frac{4 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1}{\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)^2}$

questions.q: Capacitance of an isolated conducting sphere of radius ${R}_{1}$~becomes $n$~times when it is enclosed by a concentric conducting sphere of radius ${R}_{2}$~connected to earth. The ratio of their radii  \left(\dfrac{R2}{R1}\right)$& is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capacitance of isolated conducting sphere& $C = 4\pi{ε}_{0}{R}_{1}$

By enclosing inside another sphere of radius~${R}_{2}$, new capacitance~$C^{'} = 4\pi{ε}_{0}{R}_{1}{R}_{2} \left({R}_{2} - {R}_{1}\right)

Given:~$4$\pi{ε}_{0}{R}_{1}{R}_{2}\left({R}_{2} - {R}_{1}\right) =$n $\times$4$\pi{ε}_{0}{R}_{1}

$⇒ {R}_{2}\left({R}_{2} - {R}_{1}\right) =$n ⇒ $\dfrac{R2}{R1}\left(\dfrac{R2}{R1} -$1\right) = n$

$⇒ $\dfrac{R2}{R1} =$n$\dfrac{R2}{R1} -$n ⇒ $\dfrac{R2}{R1} =$n \left(n - 1\right)

$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has plates of area A separated by distance $d$ between them. It is filled with a dielectric which has a dielectric constant that varies as $K \left(x\right) = {K}_{0} \left($1 + \alphax\right)$ where $x$ is the distance measured from one of the plates. If \left(\alphad\right)< < 1, the total capacitance of the system is best given by the expression:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capacitance of element, $d C = \dfrac{{K}_{0}\left(1 + \alphax\right){ε}_{0}A}{dx}$
$∫ \dfrac{1}{d C} = {∫}_{0}^{d}\dfrac{dx}{{K}_{0}{ε}_{0}A\left(1 + \alphax\right)}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{K}_{0}{ε}_{0}A\alpha}ln \left(1 + \alphad\right)$
Given $\alphad ≪ 1$
$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{K}_{0}{ε}_{0}A\alpha} \left(\alphad - $\dfrac{{α}^{2}d^{2}}{2}\right)
$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{d}{{K}_{0}{ε}_{0}A} \left(1 - \dfrac{\alphad}{2}\right)$
$⇒ C = \dfrac{{K}_{0}{ε}_{0}A}{d} \left(1 + \dfrac{\alphad}{2}\right)$

The effective capacitance between points A and B, when the space between the parallel plates of $C_1$ capacitor is filled with a dielectric medium having dielectric constant of 4, is :

$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{C}_1=4 \mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{C}_1=4 \times 5=20 \mu \mathrm{~F} \\ & \mathrm{C}_2=\mathrm{C}_3=5 \mu \mathrm{~F}

Correct Option (3)

questions.q: The distance between two plates of a capacitor is $d$ and its capacitance is ${C}_{1}$, when air is the medium between the plates. If a metal sheet of thickness $\dfrac{2d}{3}$ and of the same area as plate is introduced between the plates, the capacitance of the capacitor becomes~${C}_{2}$ . The ratio $\dfrac{C2}{C1}$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula of capacitance is& ${C}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d}\right)

The dielectric constant of metal sheet is~${K}_{metal} = $\infty

The new value of capacitance is~

${C}_{2} = $\dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d - t + \dfrac{t}{Kmetal}} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d - \dfrac{2d}{3} + 0} =$3{C}_{1}$

Clearly, the ratio,

\dfrac{C2}{C1} = \dfrac{3{C}_{1}}{C1} =$3: 1$

$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has plate of length $l$,~width $w$ and separation of plates is $d$. It is connected to a battery of emf~$V$. A dielectric slab of the same thickness $d$ and of dielectric constant~$K = 4$ is being inserted between the plates of the capacitor. At what length of the slab inside plates, will the energy stored in the capacitor be two times the initial energy stored?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Length of plate of parallel plate capacitor is& $l$

Width of plate~is~$w$

Separation of plates is $d$.

Emf of battery is~$V$

Thickness of dielectric slab is~$d$

Dielectric constant of slab is~$K = 4$

Capacitance of capacitor before the insertion of dielectric slab is~

${C}_{0} = \dfrac{A{ε}_{0}}{d} = \dfrac{wl{ε}_{0}}{d} . . . ( 1 )$

Energy~stored in the capacitor before the insertion of dielectrics is given by,

${U}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{2}{C}_{0}V^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{wl{ε}_{0}}{d}\right)V^{2} . . . ( 2 )$

Suppose that, the slab is inside the plate at $y$~distance, therefore, it becomes the combination of two capacitors one with air with length $( l - y )$ and another with dielectric with length~$y$~as shown in diagram.

Now the capacitance of capacitor in parallel combination is given by,

$C = {C}_{1} + {C}_{2} . . . ( 3 )$

Where,

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{w ( l - y ) {ε}_{0}}{d} . . . ( 4 )$

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{wyK{ε}_{0}}{d} . . . ( 5 )$

Now energy stored in this combination of capacitor is given by

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} ( {C}_{1} + {C}_{2} ) V^{2} . . . ( 6 )$

Now according to the given condition,

$2{U}_{0} = U$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}{C}_{0}V^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({C}_{1} + {C}_{2}\right)V^{2}$

$⇒ 2{C}_{0} = {C}_{1} + {C}_{2}$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}wl}{d}\right) = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}Kwy}{d} + \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}w ( l - y )}{d}$

$⇒ 2l = Ky + l - y$

$⇒ l = 4y - y = 3y$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{l}{3}$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor having capacitance $12pF$ is charged by a battery to a potential difference of $10V$ between its plates. The charging battery is now disconnected and a porcelain slab of dielectric constant $6.5$ is slipped between the plates. The work done by the capacitor on the slab is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial energy of capacitor

${U}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{q2}{c}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{120 \times 120}{12} = 600pJ$

Since battery is disconnected so charge remain same. Final energy of capacitor

~${U}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{q2}{ck}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{120 \times 120}{12 \times 6 . 5} = 92pJ$

$W + {U}_{f} = {U}_{i}$
$W = 508pJ$

questions.q: In the given figure the total charge stored in the combination of capacitors is $100 µ C$. The value of ‘$x$’ is ______________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
All the capacitors are in parallel combination and therefore potential drop across each capacitor would be the same.

Charge on the capacitor can be written as,& $Q = CV$.

The charge on~${C}_{1}$~is~${Q}_{1} = 2 \times 10 = 20\mu C$

The charge on~${C}_{2}$~is~${Q}_{2} = x \times 10 = 10x\mu C$

The charge on~${C}_{3}$~is~${Q}_{3} = 3 \times 10 = 30\mu C$

By the given data.

${C}_{1} + {C}_{2} + {C}_{3} = 100\mu C$

$⇒ 10\left(2 + x + 3\right) = 100$

$⇒ x = 5$

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $50pF$ is charged by $100V$ source. It is then connected to another uncharged identical capacitor. Electrostatic energy loss in the process is____~$nJ$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial charge on first capacitor will be,& $Q = CV$

As the second capacitor is identical to the first one, hence potential drop across both capacitor will be equal to~$\dfrac{V}{2}$.

Now, loss of energy,~$\Delta H = {U}_{i} - {U}_{f}$

$⇒ \Delta H = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2C\right) \times \left(\dfrac{V}{2}\right)2$

$⇒ \Delta H = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}CV^{2}⇒ \Delta H = \dfrac{1}{4}CV^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 50 \times {10}^{- 12} \times {100}^{2} = 125 \times {10}^{- 9}J = 125nJ$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has charge $5 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$. A dielectric slab is inserted between the plates and almost fills the space between the plates. If the induced charge on one face of the slab is $4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$ then the dielectric constant of the slab is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathrm{Q}\left(1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{~K}}\right) \\ & 4 \times 10^{-6}=5 \times 10^{-6}\left(1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{~K}}\right) \\ & 1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{~K}}=\frac{4}{5} \\ & \mathrm{~K}=5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Three capacitors of capacitances $25 \mu \mathrm{F}, 30 \mu \mathrm{F}$ and $45 \mu \mathrm{F}$ are connected in parallel to a supply of $100 \mathrm{~V}$. Energy stored in the above combination is E. When these capacitors are connected in series to the same supply, the stored energy is $\frac{9}{x} \mathrm{E}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In parallel combination : Potential difference is same across all
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Energy }=\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2+\mathrm{C}_3\right) \mathrm{V}^2 \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(25+30+45) \times(100)^2 \times 10^{-6}=0.5=\mathrm{E}
\end{aligned}$
In series combination: Charge is same on all.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_3}=\frac{1}{25}+\frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{45} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}=\frac{(18+15+10)}{450}=\frac{43}{450} \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}=\frac{450}{43} \\
& \text { Energy }=\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_1}+\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_2}+\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_3} \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2}\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_3}\right] \\
& \frac{\left(\mathrm{V} \times \mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}\right)^2}{2} \times \frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2 \mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}{2} \\
& \frac{(100)^2}{2} \times \frac{450}{43} \times 10^{-6} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{4.5}{86}=\frac{9}{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{E}=\frac{9}{\mathrm{x}} \times 0.5 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=86
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A capacitor of $50\muF$ is connected in a circuit as shown in figure. The charge on the upper plate of the capacitor is _________~$\muC .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At steady state current through branch of capacitor is zero. Potential difference across capacitor is $2V .$~So, $q = 50 \times 2 = 100\muC$

$i = \dfrac{6}{( 2 + 2 + 2 ) \times {10}^{3}} = 1 \times {10}^{- 3}Amp$
${V}_{A, B} =$ potential across $50\muF$
${V}_{A, B} = i \times 2 \times {10}^{3} = 1 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 2 \times {10}^{3} = 2$~volt
Charge on $50\muF$
$q = CV = 50 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 2 ⇒ 100 \times {10}^{- 6}C = 100\muC$
